Gas Line Work Beginning on Ooltewah-Ringgold Road 🚧
 Construction on a new underground regulator station and pipeline serving the Collegedale area is scheduled to begin the week of September 14 (this week). If you're traveling through the area, you may start seeing crews and equipment out soon, if not already.
 The project is part of a pressure improvement program approved by the Collegedale City Commission in August. Crews will connect new pipeline into the existing gas line near Bill Reed Road/Wellesley Drive area, run pipe north along Ooltewah-Ringgold Road to a new regulator station being built near the Apison Pike intersection, then continue the pipe past Apison Pike to reconnect with the existing line further north. The system will be tested before going into service.
 What to expect:
 ▪️No full road closures — single-lane traffic will be maintained
 ▪️Short (~200 ft) lane restrictions that shift as work progresses
 ▪️All business and property entrances will stay open
 ▪️Work may occasionally continue into weekends
 Traffic control is being coordinated with TDOT for your safety.
 Stay updated: www.collegedaletn.gov/chattanooga_gas_company_eas…/index.php
 Questions? Call us at (423) 396-3135!

🥧 FROM CULINARY SCHOOL TO RED BANK: THE SWEET STORY BEHIND PIE R SQUARE
 RED BANK, TN — Sometimes the best local businesses begin with a simple idea: “We need one of those here.”
 For Pie R Square, that idea was pie — real, homemade, from-scratch pie — and nearly eight years later, that vision has become a Red Bank favorite.
 Located at 4403 Dayton Blvd., Pie R Square got its start after the owner’s daughter attended culinary school in Atlanta and worked at a pie shop after graduation. When she returned home to Chattanooga, she decided our community needed a pie shop of its own.
 So, she started creating her own pies — from the crust to the filling to the toppings — everything homemade.
 What began on a small scale at local farmers markets has grown into a storefront right here in Red Bank, where Pie R Square has been serving up sweet and savory creations for nearly eight years.
 🥧 Something New Every Week
 Pie lovers can find a weekly rotating menu of 4-inch pies, making it easy to try different flavors throughout the year.
 And if you have a gathering, celebration, or just a serious craving, you can order a 9-inch pie with two days' advance notice.
 One flavor that deserves a special mention? Their coconut pie. 🥥🥧
 If you've ever had a homemade coconut pie that reminds you of Grandma's kitchen, you know exactly what we're talking about. Pie R Square's coconut pie tastes just like Grandma's! It's the kind of pie that brings back memories with the very first bite.
 🍗 Don't Forget the Savory Pies!
 Pie isn't just for dessert!
 Pie R Square also offers frozen chicken pot pies that are perfect to grab for an easy dinner at home or keep on hand for a special occasion. Just because dinner is quick doesn't mean it can't be delicious.
 🎃 Thanksgiving Is Coming!
 Starting November 1st, Pie R Square will begin taking Thanksgiving orders with a special holiday menu featuring both sweet and savory pies.
 And yes, the classics will be there! 🎃
 You'll be able to order their pumpkin pie along with their pumpkin cream cheese pie — a customer favorite that's truly something special.
 Whether you're looking for a traditional Thanksgiving dessert or want to bring something unexpected to the holiday table, Pie R Square will have plenty of options.
 🎉 More Than Just Pie
 Pie R Square also offers catering for weddings, business events, parties, celebrations, and other special occasions.
 Need something unique for your next event? Give them a call and see what they can create!
 From culinary school in Atlanta, to farmers markets around Chattanooga, to a storefront right here in Red Bank, the story of Pie R Square is one of a family turning a passion into a local business — one homemade pie at a time. ❤️
 📍 Pie R Square
 4403 Dayton Blvd.
 Chattanooga, TN
 🕒 Hours:
 Wednesday–Saturday: 12:00 PM–7:00 PM
 Sunday–Tuesday: Closed
 📱 Follow Pie R Square on Facebook & Instagram: @Piersquare2
 🥧 Red Bank has a pie shop. And we're pretty lucky to have it.

Did you know that Chattanooga has been recognized as a Tree City for over 34 years?
 Our city’s urban canopy isn’t just beautiful—it’s an essential public resource that protects our environment, cools our neighborhoods, cleans our air, and keeps Chattanooga healthy and vibrant for everyone. 
 The City of Chattanooga’s Urban Forestry team is working hard every day to:
 * protect and maintain trees across all neighborhoods
 * review construction permits to safeguard existing tree canopy
 * execute multi-year planting initiatives to ensure every resident enjoys the benefits of green spaces
 If you have a concern about a public tree or want to request a new tree planted in your neighborhood? You can submit tree service and planting requests directly through 311!
 #CHA311 #chattanooga #TreeCityUSA

🎨 Happy National Arts in Education Week! 🎭🎶🩰
 This week, ArtsBuild celebrates the teachers who help young people discover the power of creativity.
 Arts teachers do so much more than teach us how to paint, play an instrument, dance, perform, or create. They help us find our voices, build confidence, take risks, see the world differently, and discover talents we may not have known we had. For many of us, an arts teacher was one of the first people to truly see something special in us.
 At ArtsBuild, we believe every young person deserves access to meaningful arts experiences and great arts education. Through Imagine! and our other arts education initiatives, we work alongside Hamilton County educators and cultural partners to make the arts part of learning for thousands of students each year.
 Now we want to hear from you! ❤️
 Who was an arts teacher who made a difference in your life? Maybe it was your elementary school art teacher, band director, choir teacher, theater teacher, dance instructor, or someone who simply encouraged you to create.
 Give them a shout-out in the comments and tell us what made them special!

Save the date for CIVIQ: A Speaker Series Honoring Robert Taylor!
 CIVIQ is a free speaker series showcasing national and international ideas in urban design and creating space for conversations about how cities can approach the challenges facing their communities.
 On October 29, CIVIQ welcomes Carol Coletta for a timely conversation about Chattanooga’s riverfront: “Evergreen for Everyone, Everyday: Is It Possible?”
 Carol Coletta is a national leader in civic design and public innovation. As president and CEO of Memphis River Parks Partnership, she led a new riverfront concept plan, the renaming and redesign of two parks, the development of a five-mile bike-pedestrian trail, and the design and construction of Tom Lee Park, an internationally acclaimed riverfront park in Memphis.
 With Chattanooga preparing to enter the next phase of its riverfront parks, this is a conversation worth hearing. Come hear Coletta’s perspective and consider what’s possible for Chattanooga’s riverfront. 
 📍 Downtown Branch - Chattanooga Public Library
 📅 October 29, 5:30-7:00 PM
 🎟️ RSVP: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/civiq-a-speaker-series-honorin…

items.content_text:
Greenway Farm Garden Project. 
 Looking fantastic at Greenway Farm. 
 In 1988, a few local gardeners asked Dr. Spangler if they could plant a garden on his 160-acre farmland—what is now Greenway Farm Park. Delighted by the idea, he had his caretaker plow a plot so Hixson-area residents could grow their own food.
 In 1990, the City of Chattanooga purchased the land, and the Greenway Farm Gardeners continued under the North Chickamauga Conservatory. In 2025, they became an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit: the Greenway Farm Garden Project. Thanks to a lease with the City of Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors, their mission continues.
 The gardeners come from all around and share a passion for growing, teaching, and preserving both Greenway Farm Park and traditional gardening practices for future generations.
 Free educational sessions are offered on the second Saturday of every month from 10:00–11:00 AM, right next to the gardens.
 Visitors are welcome to stop by anytime, introduce themselves to the gardeners (who are happy to show people around), or contact the president, Sheri Steele, at sheristeele2020@gmail.com for open plots and information.  
 *Note their next class is Oct 10th focusing on winter prep for gardens*

items.content_text:
PARK IMPROVEMENTS | THANK YOU, HAMILTON COUNTY!
 Ooltewah Youth Association would like to give a big THANK YOU to the Hamilton County Tennessee Parks & Recreation Department for their continued partnership and investment in our community.
 Two recent projects are great examples of what can happen when the County and OYA work together:
 ⚾ East Hamilton Park
 OYA was fortunate to purchase the large baseballs that were previously displayed outside the Chattanooga Lookouts stadium. Hamilton County Parks & Recreation helped get them set in place at East Hamilton Park, giving these pieces of local baseball history a new home. We hope they become a fun part of the park that players and families enjoy for many years to come.
 🔨 Standifer Gap Park – Field 3
 The fencing on Field 3 has also been replaced. Hamilton County provided the funding for the new fencing, while OYA managed the project from start to finish.
 These improvements are about more than baseball fields and fences. They are investments in places where kids play, families gather, and memories are made.
 We truly appreciate Hamilton County Parks & Recreation and their willingness to partner with OYA as we continue improving the facilities that serve our kids and our community.
 Thank you for investing in Ooltewah and in youth sports!
 #OYA #OoltewahYouthAssociation #HamiltonCounty #ParkImprovements #YouthSports #Ooltewah #CommunityPartnership

 From student success and hands-on learning to nationally recognized research, community engagement and nearly $500 million in capital projects, the University is building on its purpose while preparing for the future.
 Following the address, the UTC community came together on Terrell Owens Way to celebrate 140 years with the UTC Alma Mater, a ceremonial birthday cake cutting with Chancellor Bruce and UT System President Randy Boyd, and an afternoon of birthday fun. 🎂🎉
 Here’s to 140 years of Mocs making an impact and to the generations still to come.
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/state-of-the-university-2026-140-ye…/

items.title: So excited to see Chattanooga named one of the five best trail towns in America, alongside four other amazing destinatio...
items.content_text:
So excited to see Chattanooga named one of the five best trail towns in America, alongside four other amazing destinations.
 We're grateful to our team members who work tirelessly to keep Chattanooga at the forefront of writers' and editors' minds as they curate these lists!
 Read more: https://www.visitchattanooga.com/…/outside-magazine-names-…/ 
 #Chattanooga #travelandtourism | Tennessee Vacation | Outside Magazine
Outside Magazine named Chattanooga one of the five best trail towns in America.
 The other four are Bend, Boulder, Marquette, and Mill Valley. Mill Valley has about 14,000 people. Chattanooga has 194,000 (Metro pop is way bigger). Being ten minutes from a trailhead is normal when you live in a town of 14,000. It is not normal here, and that is the whole story.
 We have never pitched Chattanooga as a city with great outdoor access. That framing puts nature somewhere else. Here it is not somewhere else. The mountains and the river got here first, and the city had to work around them.
 Here is how it came together, because these stories do not assemble themselves.
 Erin McGrady at Authentic Story Co. came to us looking for insider knowledge, not a press kit. Ava Rymer went straight to the running community and got Peter Hagemeyer at Fast Break Athletics to answer eight questions on a brutal deadline. Susan Harris connected us to Ginny Smith at Bad Beard Events, who is directing the 2027 UTMB Ultra-Trail Chattanooga (June 4–6, 2027). 
 “What’s unique about Chattanooga is that you can be standing downtown and within 10 or 15 minutes be at the base of Lookout Mountain via the Riverwalk, on Raccoon Mountain, at Stringer’s Ridge, or up on Signal," Smith says. 
 Congratulations to everyone who has spent decades building and protecting the trails that made this true. 
 Chattanooga Tourism Co. Chattanooga Parks and Outdoors City of Chattanooga - Government

 We can think of no person more deserving to be the first East Ridge citizen recognized under the statute than Councilman Jacky Cagle.  A lifetime of service.  A lasting legacy in #EastRidgeTN. 🤍

items.content_text:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the G20 area grew by 0.7% in the second quarter of 2026, slightly down from 0.8% in the previous quarter. 
 Among G20 economies, the contraction in Saudi Arabia deepened, with GDP falling by 4.8% in Q2 2026, following a 1.4% decline in Q1, this mainly reflected a sharp decrease in oil activities. 
 By contrast, growth rebounded strongly in Mexico, with GDP increasing by 1.4% in Q2 after contracting by 0.3% in Q1, and remained strong in Indonesia, at 1.3% (similar to Q1). Growth also strengthened in Türkiye, from 0.3% to 1.1%, and in Canada, from 0.1% to 0.8%, while it picked up slightly in Australia, from 0.3% to 0.4%. In France, GDP was unchanged in Q2, following a contraction of 0.2% in Q1.  
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x5Hfv | #OECDstats

🚂 Congratulations to the Tennessee Valley Railroad Museum on 65 years of preservation!
 For more than six decades, the Tennessee Valley Railroad Museum has demonstrated the power of preservation by keeping our region’s railroad history alive and accessible to future generations.
 Chattanooga’s identity and growth are inseparable from its railroad heritage, and TVRM has been an extraordinary steward of that story. Their work is a reminder that preservation is about more than protecting the past, it's about finding ways for history to remain an active and meaningful part of our lives today.
 Congratulations to the staff, volunteers, supporters, and generations of preservationists who have made 65 years possible. Here’s to many more years of keeping Chattanooga’s railroad history on track!
 https://www.wdef.com/tennessee-valley-railroad-museum-cele…/

Getting to class can be one of the most routine parts of a student’s day, but the hassle of parking, navigating Chattanooga’s heat and long walks across campus can throw that routine off. For students looking to ease these burdens, UTC offers the Mocs Express shuttle as a convenient, safe way to get around campus free of charge. 🚌 
 The Mocs Express shuttle operates a regular 13-hour route Monday through Friday, with a special Friday evening route for students to enjoy. Starting at Engel Stadium, the Mocs Express runs through campus and the neighboring streets for a complete loop of less than 30 minutes. Once the bus returns to its starting point, the route restarts.
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/your-ride-around-campus-getting-to-…/

 📅 Tuesday, September 22, 2026
 ⏰ 1:30-2:30 p.m. ET

  1 Carter St, Chattanooga, TN 37402

 At the listening session, you'll have the opportunity to discuss the emergency rules, ask questions, share concerns, and provide feedback for the permanent rulemaking process.
